texts.value: Type IV collagen is the major structural component of glomerular basement membranes (GBM), forming a 'chicken-wire' meshwork together with laminins, proteoglycans and entactin/nidogen

Canstatin, a cleavage product corresponding to the collagen alpha 2(IV) NC1 domain, possesses both anti-angiogenic and anti-tumor cell activity. It inhibits proliferation and migration of endothelial cells, reduces mitochondrial membrane potential, and induces apoptosis. Specifically induces Fas-dependent apoptosis and activates procaspase-8 and -9 activity. Ligand for alphavbeta3 and alphavbeta5 integrins

There are six type IV collagen isoforms, alpha 1(IV)-alpha 6(IV), each of which can form a triple helix structure with 2 other chains to generate type IV collagen network. Interacts with EFEMP2 (By similarity)

location.value: Secreted, extracellular space, extracellular matrix, basement membrane

texts.value: Alpha chains of type IV collagen have a non-collagenous domain (NC1) at their C-terminus, frequent interruptions of the G-X-Y repeats in the long central triple-helical domain (which may cause flexibility in the triple helix), and a short N-terminal triple-helical 7S domain
Prolines at the third position of the tripeptide repeating unit (G-X-Y) are hydroxylated in some or all of the chains

Type IV collagens contain numerous cysteine residues which are involved in inter- and intramolecular disulfide bonding. 12 of these, located in the NC1 domain, are conserved in all known type IV collagens
The trimeric structure of the NC1 domains is stabilized by covalent bonds between Lys and Met residues
Proteolytic processing produces the C-terminal NC1 peptide, canstatin

disease.diseaseId: Brain small vessel disease 2A, autosomal dominant
disease.description: An autosomal dominant cerebrovascular disorder with variable manifestations reflecting the location and severity of the vascular defect. BSVD2 features include intracranial hemorrage, fluid-filled cysts or cavities within the cerebral hemispheres, delayed psychomotor development, hemiplegia, spasticity and seizures.

texts.value: The disease is caused by variants affecting the gene represented in this entry

disease.diseaseId: Brain small vessel disease 2B, autosomal recessive
disease.description: An autosomal recessive cerebrovascular disorder characterized by global developmental delay, impaired intellectual development with poor or absent speech, seizures, and spastic quadriplegia. Neurologic abnormalities appear in infancy or the first years of life. Brain imaging may show colpocephaly, brain atrophy, white matter abnormalities, and signs of vascular injury.

disease.description: A pathological condition characterized by bleeding into one or both cerebral hemispheres including the basal ganglia and the cerebral cortex. It is often associated with hypertension and craniocerebral trauma. Intracerebral bleeding is a common cause of stroke.
